result.summary: I've asked the contractor and the tenant what happened with the lock job. The contractor, Oliver Sawyer, phoned the tenant on 18 Nov to say he was on his way with two locks. By 19 Nov there was still no report on the work (event 012). I emailed the contractor asking whether he attended, what he found, whether he repaired or replaced the lock, and what it cost. I texted the tenant to ask whether the lock now works, and put the ticket on hold until 20 Nov to chase them.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 011 shows the contractor was on his way on 18 Nov. Event 012 says there's no record of the work. The contractor and the tenant can both say what happened, so asking them is the right step before escalating. The lock is stiff but still works, so this isn't an emergency. I kept the ticket at 'scheduling' because nothing confirms the contractor actually turned up.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The missing information can come straight from the contractor or tenant. Nothing is overdue twice yet.
